clue.text: Cat causes other creatures great suffering

parts.note: tortoises are creatures other than cats, shelled reptiles
hell is a byword for extreme torment

explanation.surface: A cat is blamed for making other animals miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoiseshell is a cat with a mottled black, orange and cream coat.

clue.text: Ladies and gentlemen of the audience, lyric content has been replaced by a true revolutionary artist

indicators.note: what listeners in an audience hear, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: the ladies' and the gentlemen's are two public toilets, two loos in British slang

indicators.note: the emptied word lyric now holds new filling in place of its old middle
with its content gone, only the outside letters of lyric stay in place
revolutionary hints that the letters of a true are turned over and reordered

explanation.surface: A compere addresses the crowd while a song's words are swapped for something radical.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is British slang for toilet, so the ladies' and the gents' are two of them. 'Content' empties the word lyric to its ends, and 'revolutionary' reorders a true before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec was a French painter and poster artist of Montmartre.

clue.text: Stir up right and throw out of office

parts.note: to oust is to remove someone from a position

explanation.surface: A rebellion begins with agitation and the removal of a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse or disturb someone into action.

clue.text: As you like it, part of Florida

definitions.meaning: a role in Shakespeare's comedy As You Like It, its romantic hero
a city of the US state of Florida, home of theme parks

explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is the hero of As You Like It and also a large city in central Florida.

clue.text: Loveless, 20, married and ruined

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, so the letter O is dropped

parts.note: twenty as a number is a score
wed means married

explanation.surface: Someone without love, on a number, has married and come to grief.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' looks like a cross-reference to 20 across (DEUCE), but here it is just the number twenty, a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwed is slang for done for or thoroughly wrecked.

clue.text: Break strike a great success

parts.note: to smash is to break
to hit is to strike

explanation.surface: Breaking and striking things leads to triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash hit is a hugely popular show, song or film, a runaway triumph.

clue.text: May be ten out of ten are docile, playing in friendly agreement

indicators.note: the first word stands out of, around, the second ten
the first ten only may be ten, signalling its letters are rearranged
playing suggests the letters of are docile are being moved about

explanation.surface: Perfect marks for docile pupils who play nicely together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be' rearranges the first ten, which 'out of' then wraps round the second ten; 'playing' reorders are docile to finish the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Entente Cordiale was the 1904 Anglo-French accord, and the phrase now means any cordial understanding.

clue.text: Interesting ale brewed in 22

definitions.note: 22 down is COLON, part of the bowel

indicators.note: ale is brewed, and the word suggests these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A fascinating beer brewed inside the gut.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference to 22 down, COLON; strictly the colon is only part of the large intestine.
explanation.definitionFit: The colon is the main section of the large bowel, so the setter treats them as one.

clue.text: Two in three, perhaps, going north, diced with death: one reason for judgement

parts.note: two to three is an example of a ratio

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means the word diced is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
death is the end
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gambler weighs the odds and risks death rolling dice before a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going north' turns DICED to DECID. RATIO DECIDENDI is a law term: the legal principle on which a court's decision rests.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for the reason for deciding: the principle of law that a court's ruling rests on.

clue.text: USA twice interfered with Libyan leader: nothing new there

indicators.note: interfered with suggests the doubled letters are disturbed and reordered
twice says the word USA is taken two times over
the leader of Libyan is its opening letter

explanation.surface: America meddles in Libya again, which surprises nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: As usual describes things happening in the normal, unremarkable way.

clue.text: Source of energy about player

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A tale about a performer drawing power from somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor generates power, so it is a source of energy.

clue.text: It could be kind now to search me

indicators.note: the letters that follow could be something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Being kind now would be a good way to look into me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It could be' rearranges KIND NOW TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Search me is an idiom for having no idea of the answer.

clue.text: Bracket partner's joint

definitions.meaning: Dame Hilda Bracket's stage partner in the British drag act ... and Bracket was Dr Evadne ...
a pivoting joint on a door or lid

explanation.walkthrough: Hinge and Bracket were a British comic drag duo playing two genteel elderly ladies; 'bracket' looks like a shelf support.
explanation.definitionFit: Evadne Hinge partnered Hilda Bracket, and a hinge is the movable joint of a door.

clue.text: Perhaps a feature of the Katmandu sky

definitions.text: Perhaps a feature of the Katmandu sky

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Evening light might be a characteristic of the sky over Nepal's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Perhaps' cannot stand for the answer; the whole clue defines it, as dusk is a feature of any evening sky, Katmandu's included.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is something you could see in the sky above Katmandu each evening.

clue.text: Flyer's deal with greedy person takes a very long time

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber, a kind of wood
a pig is a glutton
an eon is an age

explanation.surface: An aviator arranges a deal with a glutton that drags on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' looks like a verb or a bargain, but it is softwood timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodpigeon is a common large bird, and any bird is a flyer.

clue.text: I left Suzie wet in a dominant state

indicators.note: left means the letter is left out of the name

parts.note: taken as written
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: I walked out on a soaked Suzie in a power struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' takes the I out of SUZIE to give SUZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A suzerain is a sovereign state that controls another state's foreign affairs.

clue.text: Black and white firm sells our product

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: the product of the letters is a new arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A monochrome company markets its own goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in black and white only has no colour in it.

clue.text: Do not interfere with auditor's credit in trading places

indicators.note: the two parts of the word swap their positions
an auditor is a listener, so this is how the word comes across to the ear

parts.note: to credit a story is to believe it

explanation.surface: Leave the accountant's figures alone during the share swap.
explanation.walkthrough: Heard, the word for 'credit' splits as 'be' plus 'leave'; 'in trading places' swaps the two halves. 'Auditor' looks like an accountant, but is a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave be means to let something alone and not meddle with it.

clue.text: You are rumoured to be involved with Masai warrior

indicators.note: with here means the jumbled letters keep the other piece among them
involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed
something rumoured is passed on by word of mouth, so these words are heard

parts.note: said quickly, you are sounds like the letters U R

explanation.surface: Gossip says you have joined up with an East African warrior people.
explanation.walkthrough: The Masai are an East African people; 'involved' reorders their name, which then takes the sounded letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of the military caste of feudal Japan.

clue.text: Wine went up

definitions.meaning: pink wine, made with brief contact with red grape skins
past tense of to ascend or climb

explanation.definitionFit: Rosé is a pink wine, and rose is the past tense of rise, to ascend.

clue.text: Devil's tie?

definitions.meaning: the ... is an old euphemism for the devil, as in what the ...
in tennis, forty-all is a tied score

explanation.definitionFit: Deuce is an oath-word for the devil and the tennis term for a level score at forty all.

clue.text: Type that may be 5th and 7th in military academy

definitions.text: Type that may be 5th and 7th in military academy

indicators.note: the letters may be this when rearranged, so they are reordered
the fifth letter of military
the seventh letter of military

explanation.surface: A trainee soldier is the kind of person one finds in officer school.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifth and seventh letters of MILITARY are T and R; 'may be' rearranges them with ACADEMY.
explanation.definitionFit: An army cadet is a young person in training for the army, the sort found at a military school.

clue.text: Pass on:

definitions.note: the clue's own punctuation mark is the thing defined

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note telling someone to hand something along.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the printed colon itself, which looks like mere punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark of two stacked dots is called a colon.

clue.text: Managed to come back with speed to provide the commentary

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to run something is to manage it
rate means speed

explanation.surface: A commentator returns quickly to describe the action.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to give a spoken account, as a commentator does.

clue.text: Once more pick up another cheque, useful ultimately to make money

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each word

parts.note: to earn is to make money

explanation.surface: Collect a second cheque, which is handy for getting paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' takes the last letters of ANOTHER CHEQUE USEFUL, giving R, E and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To relearn is to acquire a skill or knowledge again.

clue.text: Trouble in the loo

parts.note: taken as written
a public convenience is a toilet, in British usage

explanation.surface: Something going wrong in the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: A public convenience is the British term for a public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconvenience means bother or difficulty caused to someone.
